children: added more than 30% on Tuesday to hit a new 52-week high after the glucose monitoring equipment maker reported higher-than-expected Q3 2026 results and raised its full-year outlook, prompting Raymond James to upgrade the stock.

The Germantown, Maryland-based MedTech reported a $0.50 GAAP loss per share on $19.6M in revenue for the quarter, beating Street forecasts by $0.02 and $3.4M, respectively, while its revised 2026 outlook for net revenue at $68M-$70M exceeded the $64M
Raymond James analyst Jayson Bedford upgraded Senseonics
to Market Perform from Underperform, noting that the company has made headway both with its U.S. execution and capital needs, concerns over which led to his prior bearish view.

“Momentum in the U.S. business has exceeded our expectations, and investors have shown a greater willingness to fund a business that continues to burn significant cash,” Bedford wrote, adding that those factors have reduced the downside risks for the stock.

While the analyst remains concerned about the sustainability of the company’s economics and its path toward profitability, he argued that “the current momentum and initial enthusiasm over the pipeline will overshadow these concerns in the near-term.”

However, Stifel’s Jonathan Block retained his Hold rating on SENS, noting that despite being supportive of the company’s direct sales strategy, he is more concerned about its costs and the time Senseonics
could take to record positive free cash flow.

title: Senseonics hits 52-week high as Raymond James upgrades on Q3 beat and raise
